title: The point fibre functor preserves derived tensor at all coefficient stages
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\ell\ne p$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension inside a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $\mathcal O_E$ be its valuation ring and $\varpi_E$ a uniformizer, and let $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use the point coefficient categories and the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the finite-Tor subcategory of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the derived tensor product of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], completed at the integral stage and formed at a common finite coefficient stage at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Fib}_s(M)\otimes^L_\Lambda\operatorname{Fib}_s(N).
$$
It is natural in $M,N$, carries the coefficient unit to $\Lambda$, and respects the associativity, symmetry and unit constraints of derived tensor. It commutes with finite reduction and scalar extension in these coefficient constructions.
